newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy studying help for car industry - minister.
newsitem.headline: Italy studying help for car industry - minister.

text.p: Italy's government is studying measures to help its car industry, but no measures are imminent, said Italian foreign trade minister Augusto Fantozzi on Tuesday.
"The government is studying intervention in the car industry, even of a fiscal nature," Fantozzi said.
"Intervention is needed for the car industry, whether of a financial and fiscal nature or in the form of investment", Fantozzi said while attending the Turin car week.
"In any case the eventual incentives are not under my control. It is the finance minister that must decide this," he added.

The Italian car market has remained depressed since the European car market hit a low point in 1993, although most other major European car markets including Germany, Britain and France have all recovered from 1993 levels.
